curriculum.title: HTML Step 8: Page Layout Tags
curriculum.description: Shape a page with header, nav, main, section, article, aside and footer, learn why they beat a pile of divs, and build a whole page.

avatar.handoff_to_practice: Your turn. Fill in the TODO lines.

lessons.title: Header and Footer
lessons.goal: to add a header and a footer to a page.

avatar.text: Most websites have a top part and a bottom part. HTML has special tags for them!

code_example.code:
Ada's Pets

Welcome to my page about pets.

Made by Ada, 2026
code_example.description: Watch a page get a top and a bottom.
code_example.explanation: Lines 1 to 3 are the header: the top part of the page, with its title. The locked CSS paints it blue.

avatar.text: Lines 5 to 7 are the footer: the bottom of the page, for things like who made it. Header at the top, footer at the bottom.

question.question: Where does a header usually go?
options: At the top of the page
In the middle of a paragraph
question.answer: At the top of the page
question.explanation: Yes! The header is the top part.

avatar.on_correct: Yes! The header is the top part.
avatar.on_wrong: Not quite. The header is the top part of the page.

question.question: A footer is a good place to say who made the page.

avatar.on_wrong: Not quite. Footers often say who made the page.

question.question: Your turn: add a footer at the bottom with a paragraph that says Made by Leo. Tap Run to test it, then Submit.
question.explanation: Remember: lines 5 to 7 are the footer.

code_example.code:
Ada's Pets

Welcome to my page about pets.

Made by Ada, 2026
code_example.explanation: Remember: lines 5 to 7 are the footer.
code_example.starterCode:
Leo's Robots

I build robots from boxes.
code_example.solutionCode:
Leo's Robots

I build robots from boxes.

Made by Leo

avatar.before_demo: Before you try, one quick look at the example.
avatar.handoff: Got it? I'll clear the example now.
avatar.on_correct: Great! Your page has a top and a bottom.
avatar.on_wrong: Not yet. Open a footer, put a p with Made by Leo inside it, then close the footer.

retry.hint: Copy Ada's footer and change the words.

points: header is the top of the page.
Each one wraps the parts inside it.

avatar.text: Nice work! Here's what you learned.
Next up: a menu of links.

lessons.title: The Menu: nav
lessons.goal: to group a site's menu links in a nav.

avatar.text: How do you get around a website? With a menu. In HTML, the menu goes in a nav.

code_example.description: Watch a menu appear in the header.
code_example.explanation: Lines 3 to 6 are a nav: the menu of links that helps people move around the site.

avatar.text: The nav sits inside the header here, so the menu is at the top. Screen readers can jump straight to the nav.

question.question: What belongs in a nav?
question.explanation: Yes! The nav holds the menu.

avatar.on_correct: Yes! The nav holds the menu.
avatar.on_wrong: Not quite. A nav holds the menu links.

question.question: Screen readers can jump straight to the nav.
question.explanation: Correct! That helps people find the menu fast.

avatar.on_correct: Correct! That helps people find the menu fast.
avatar.on_wrong: Not quite. They can jump right to it.

question.question: Your turn: put the Games and Books links inside a nav, inside the header. Tap Run to test it, then Submit.
question.explanation: Remember: lines 3 to 6 put the links in a nav.

code_example.explanation: Remember: lines 3 to 6 put the links in a nav.
code_example.starterCode:
Mia's Corner

Games Books

avatar.before_demo: Before you try, one quick look at the example.
avatar.handoff: Got it? I'll clear the example now.
avatar.on_correct: Brilliant! Mia's site has a menu.
avatar.on_wrong: Not yet. Put an opening nav above the Games link, and a closing nav below the Books link.

retry.hint: Open nav before the first link, close it after the second.

points: It often sits in the header.
It helps people find their way.

avatar.text: Great job! Here's what you learned.
Next up: the main part of the page.

lessons.title: Main and Section
lessons.goal: to put the main content in main, split into sections.

avatar.text: Between the header and the footer is the most important part: the main content.

code_example.code:
Zoo Guide

Lions

Lions sleep up to 20 hours a day.

Zebras

Every zebra has different stripes.
code_example.description: Watch the main part fill with sections.
code_example.explanation: Line 4 opens main: the main content of the page. A page has only one main.

avatar.text: Inside main, each section is one topic with its own heading: Lions, then Zebras. One main, many sections.

question.question: How many main elements should a page have?

avatar.on_wrong: Not quite. A page has only one main.

retry.hint: How many mains did the Zoo Guide have?

question.question: A section is one topic, usually with its own heading.

avatar.on_wrong: Not quite. Each section is one topic with a heading.

retry.hint: What did each section start with?

question.question: Your turn: add a second section inside main, with an h2 Penguins and the paragraph Penguins can't fly, but they swim fast. Tap Run to test it, then Submit.
question.explanation: Remember: each section has a heading and its own content.

code_example.code:
Zoo Guide

Lions

Lions sleep up to 20 hours a day.

Zebras

Every zebra has different stripes.
code_example.explanation: Remember: each section has a heading and its own content.
code_example.starterCode:
Bird Guide

Owls

Owls can turn their heads very far.
code_example.solutionCode:
Bird Guide

Owls

Owls can turn their heads very far.

Penguins

Penguins can't fly, but they swim fast.

domChecks.text: Penguins can't fly, but they swim fast.

avatar.before_demo: Before you try, one quick look at the example.
avatar.handoff: Got it? I'll clear the example now.
avatar.on_wrong: Not yet. Copy the Owls section inside main, then change the heading and the paragraph.

retry.hint: Copy the whole Owls section and change the words.

points: A page has only one main.
Each section is one topic with a heading.

avatar.text: Fantastic! Here's what you learned.
Next up: stories and side notes.

lessons.title: Article and Aside
lessons.goal: to mark a story with article and a side note with aside.

avatar.text: Some content stands on its own, like a story. Some is extra, like a fun fact on the side.

code_example.code:
My Trip to the Beach

We built a giant sandcastle.

Fun fact: sand is made of tiny rocks.
code_example.description: Watch a story and a side note appear.
code_example.explanation: Lines 2 to 5 are an article: something that makes sense on its own, like a story or a blog post.

avatar.text: Lines 6 to 8 are an aside: extra information on the side. The story still makes sense without it.

question.question: Which fits best in an article?
options: A blog post about your weekend
One fun fact on the side
question.answer: A blog post about your weekend
question.explanation: Yes! It makes sense on its own.

avatar.on_correct: Yes! It makes sense on its own.
avatar.on_wrong: Not quite. An article is a whole story that stands on its own.

question.question: The story needs the aside to make sense.
question.explanation: Correct, that's false. An aside is extra.

avatar.on_correct: Correct, that's false. An aside is extra.
avatar.on_wrong: Not quite. An aside is only extra information.

retry.hint: Would the beach story work without the fun fact?

question.question: Your turn: put the fun fact paragraph inside an aside. Tap Run to test it, then Submit.
question.explanation: Remember: lines 6 to 8 put the fun fact in an aside.

code_example.code:
My Trip to the Beach

We built a giant sandcastle.

Fun fact: sand is made of tiny rocks.
code_example.explanation: Remember: lines 6 to 8 put the fun fact in an aside.
code_example.starterCode:
My Visit to the Farm

I fed the goats.

Fun fact: goats have no top front teeth.
code_example.solutionCode:
My Visit to the Farm

I fed the goats.

Fun fact: goats have no top front teeth.

domChecks.text: Fun fact: goats have no top front teeth.

avatar.before_demo: Before you try, one quick look at the example.
avatar.handoff: Got it? I'll clear the example now.
avatar.on_correct: Well done! A story with a side note.
avatar.on_wrong: Not yet. Put an opening aside before the fun fact paragraph, and a closing aside after it.

retry.hint: Wrap the fun fact paragraph: aside, the paragraph, closing aside.

points: article: a whole story that stands alone.
aside: extra information on the side.
The story works without the aside.

avatar.text: Well done! Here's what you learned.
Next up: build a whole page!

lessons.title: Project: A Whole Page
lessons.goal: to build a page from layout tags, not just divs.

avatar.text: Project time! You'll build a whole page with layout tags.

code_example.code:
Kofi's Football Page

My Team

I play for the Lions.

Made by Kofi
code_example.description: Watch a whole page come together.
code_example.explanation: A whole page: header at the top, main in the middle with a section, footer at the bottom.

avatar.text: You could build this with divs, but layout tags tell browsers, search engines and screen readers what each part is for. That's why we use them.

question.question: Why use header, main and footer instead of only divs?
options: They say what each part is for
They make the page load slower
question.answer: They say what each part is for
question.explanation: Yes! They give each part a meaning.

avatar.on_correct: Yes! They give each part a meaning.
avatar.on_wrong: Not quite. Layout tags tell everyone what each part is for.

retry.hint: What do the tag names describe?

question.question: The header comes before main, and the footer comes after it.

avatar.on_wrong: Not quite. Header, then main, then footer.

question.question: Your turn: build the whole page. Follow the TODO lines from top to bottom. Tap Run to test it, then Submit.
